page_placements.theme: Training regime, data, objective and architecture shift unit-level concept alignment in vision, audio and genomic models

record.tranche_reason: The study uses network dissection to measure interpretable units and concepts in a vision model under pruning. This is a different measurement and setting from the claim's neuron-pole audit, and it bears on the claim's interpretation of neuron interpretability and regularization.
record.gate_note: The study measures network-dissection interpretability, not whether explanations predict activations on held-out examples or whether neurons have one or two jobs. Reported findings cited from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This study does not test any version. It measures how magnitude pruning, with lottery-ticket retraining, changes network-dissection interpretability in ResNet-50. Pruning removes weights but keeps the neuron count fixed, so it does not vary capacity in the sense V4 means (features versus neurons). It also does not compare architectures, regularizers or interpretability tools. The result that interpretability is unchanged until accuracy falls is a related but different finding. None of the enum values fits a study that neither tests nor uses the claim; 'discusses' is the nearest.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Sparse magnitude pruning leaves ResNet-50's network-dissection interpretability unchanged until accuracy declines, and pruning does not improve it.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses magnitude pruning with lottery-ticket fine-tuning and network dissection, rather than auditing language-model neuron poles or testing natural-language explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: Interpretability begins to decline as pruning passes the point where accuracy also declines; higher-level concepts are described as more volatile.

fits_no_version.finding: In ResNet-50 on ImageNet, magnitude pruning leaves the number of network-dissection-interpretable units and concepts unchanged until about 16.8% of weights remain. Below that, both decline along with accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing superfluous weights (at a fixed neuron count) does not change unit-level interpretability until accuracy degrades.

fits_no_version.finding: After 89% of weights are pruned, nearly 80% of originally interpretable units remain interpretable. About 70% of the units interpretable in both networks keep the same concept.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The unit-level concepts measured by network dissection largely persist through retraining after pruning.

record.peer_reviewed: ICLR 2019 Debugging Machine Learning Models Workshop
record.problems: The study covers only Resnet-50 and one sparse-pruning/fine-tuning approach. Interpretability is measured by network dissection on Broden concepts, not by testing explanations on unseen activations. Several results are described qualitatively or approximately, and no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No results-bearing findings were omitted. Figure 1's accuracy values are not recorded as rows because accuracy is a capability check rather than a measure of the claim's interpretability findings.

untested.parts: The whole version: no Qwen3-32B audit and no pole-level job shares.
The whole version: no language models, no mixture-of-experts models, no scale sweep.
The whole version: no InceptionV1 cat/car neuron, no pose reading, no recursive generalization.
No comparison of architectures, regularization or tools. No InceptionV1 estimate. Pruning keeps the neuron count fixed, so capacity in V4's sense is not varied.
The whole version: no attribution graphs and no replacement-model comparison.
The whole version: explanations are not tested on where the neuron fires.
The whole version: no simulation-based scoring.

missing.what: Absolute share of interpretable units: roughly 1000+ of the 2048 final-layer units, read off the Figure 2 axis. It is plotted only, never stated in text. This may matter to researchers comparing vision interpretable-share estimates.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's own guesses of relation 'tests', tranche T2, and V4 labels are not justified. The study never manipulates architecture, regularization or tools, and it holds the neuron count fixed. All verdict labels are removed.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B audit, pole-level job counts, and claimed percentages are not tested.
No language models, mixture-of-experts models, or scale sweep are studied.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose interpretation, and recursive generalization are not studied.

The study tests pruning-related changes in network-dissection interpretability for ResNet-50, but does not compare architectures or tools, test the InceptionV1 estimate, or isolate the causes of interpretability differences.
Attribution graphs and reconstruction without a replacement model are not tested.
Explanations are not tested for predicting activation on examples they were not written from.
Automated explanation scoring on new text is not studied.

relation.reason: Its own results are on pruning, not on any claim version. Only the discussion mentions capacity, as a possible future test.

tranche.reason: The study measures how magnitude pruning affects network-dissection interpretability in ResNet-50. It does not vary architecture, regularization or tools as V4 does, and it tests no version.

source_check.notes: Workshop paper, ResNet-50 only; dissection counts are plotted, not stated in prose. The 2048 units are the final four layers (the Figure 2 caption says 'fourth group of layers'). Pruning keeps the neuron count fixed, so the study does not bear on V4. The methods text says it removes weights with the 'highest magnitudes', probably a typo for lowest.

statements.correction: ResNet-50 on ImageNet: interpretability unchanged until 16.8% of weights remain; at 89% pruned nearly 80% of originally interpretable units stay interpretable and about 70% keep the same concept (among units interpretable in both).
